title: review: G2b fix round 2: build the repo map from the merged commit, not ROOT's checked-out tree; drop the fake nested-gate guard; record a failed refresh on the merge result (review T-0305)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain 66ff50f "Fix repomap trimming and merge gate" over dd8ab79 in git log; never drop them.
Review T-0305 on T-0302: (high) merge.py calls repomap.build(ROOT) after the fast-forward, but ROOT normally has a different branch checked out than the merge target (update-ref only), so architecture.md is generated from whatever ROOT has on disk and the header sha is ROOT's HEAD, not the merged sha. (med) gate_env sets ORCH_ROOT to the worktree for the tests-green subprocess and a comment claims a recursion guard that does not exist; tests-green.sh reads neither ORCH_TESTS_GREEN nor ORCH_ROOT, and a nested process importing orchestrator would treat the task worktree as the real root. (low) a bare except around the refresh only prints to stderr; the merge result carries no record.
Change:
1. repomap.build(root, budget_chars=4000, rev=None): when rev is given, read every orchestrator/*.py blob from that commit with `git show <rev>:<path>` (list via `git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev> -- orchestrator`) instead of the working tree, and put the short sha of rev in the header. merge.merge passes rev=<merged sha> and writes ROOT/.orchestrator/memory/architecture.md from it. Tests: test_build_from_rev_ignores_working_tree (edit a file in the working tree after committing; build(rev=HEAD) shows the committed symbols and the header sha of HEAD).
2. merge.py gate_env: stop setting ORCH_ROOT for the gate subprocess; delete the comment about a recursion guard; keep the earlier fix (the gate always runs). If test_merge's real-repo merges still recurse without it, make the recursion impossible in the test fixture instead (the scratch repo used by real_repo() must not contain a tests/ directory that imports orchestrator, or tests-green must be pointed at the scratch repo's own runner) and explain in the final message.
3. On a refresh failure merge.merge returns status 'merged' plus repomap_error = str(e)[:200] on the result dict and prints '[merge] repomap refresh failed' to stderr; daemon.report_merge already notifies with the result, so the field appears in the notification; test: test_merge_reports_repomap_error.
4. Keep every test in tests/test_repomap.py and tests/test_merge.py green.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows 66ff50f and dd8ab79 below your commit
tests/test_repomap.py::test_build_from_rev_ignores_working_tree passes; tests/test_merge.py::test_merge_reports_repomap_error passes; all earlier repomap and merge tests still pass
merge.py no longer sets ORCH_ROOT for the gate subprocess and carries no recursion-guard comment
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree within 10 minutes

comments.issue: This file imports `from orchestrator.repomap import build` without first importing `tests/_harness` (which sets ORCH_ROOT before any `from orchestrator import ...`, per _harness.py's own documented invariant). Importing `orchestrator.repomap` triggers `orchestrator/__init__.py`, which binds the module-level `ROOT` constant once, permanently, to `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` (the real repo) if ORCH_ROOT isn't set yet. Verified empirically: running `python -m unittest tests.test_repomap tests.test_merge` (the exact file order named in this task's own acceptance criteria) makes `orchestrator.merge.ROOT` bind to the real repo instead of the scratch TMP repo, so every git/build call in merge.py runs against the wrong repository. Result: test_merge_refreshes_repomap_on_py_change and test_merge_reports_repomap_error (both named in the acceptance criteria) fail/error, plus 4 other pre-existing merge tests fail, and the run balloons from 3.6s (test_merge alone, all 7 pass) to 327s for 12 tests. Running tests/test_merge.py alone: 7/7 pass in 3.6s. Running both together: 6 of 12 fail/error. This directly falsifies the acceptance bullet requiring both files' named tests to pass together, and risks tests-green.sh's 10-minute budget (bullet 4) if this ordering occurs during the real gate run.

gate_env sets IN_TESTS_GREEN ("ORCH_TESTS_GREEN") unconditionally, but nothing in the repo reads this variable (confirmed via grep across .sh/.py files) — it's dead code. The removed prior version pinned ORCH_ROOT=wt for the nested gate specifically to keep a nested tests-green run scoped to the task's scratch repo instead of re-running the full outer suite; this replacement doesn't restore that behavior, it just sets an inert marker. Low severity since it satisfies the literal acceptance text (no ORCH_ROOT, no recursion-guard comment) and isn't itself proven to cause a failure, but it's unused complexity that should either be wired to something or removed.
